The '''1998 Ballon d'Or''', given to the best [[Association football|football]] player in Europe as judged by a panel of sports journalists from [[UEFA]] member countries, was awarded to [[Zinedine Zidane]] on 22 December 1998.<ref>{{Cite web
| url        = https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/europa-poy98.html
| title      = European Footballer of the Year ("Ballon d'Or") 1998
| first      = José Luis
| last       = Pierrend
| publisher  = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF]]
| date       = 26 March 2005
| accessdate = 4 November 2013
| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20130314042124/http://rsssf.com/miscellaneous/europa-poy98.html| archivedate= 14 March 2013 | url-status= live}}</ref> On 10 November 1998, the shortlist of 50 male players compiled by a group of experts from ''[[France Football]]'' was announced.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Redacția |date=1998-11-10 |title=Adrian Ilie a fost nominalizat pentru "Balonul de Aur" |url=https://www.ziaruldeiasi.ro/stiri/adrian-ilie-a-fost-nominalizat-pentru-quotbalonul-de-aurquot--jvu.html |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=Ziarul de Iaşi - liderul presei ieşene}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1999-11-27 |title=ALL YOU PREMIER LEAGUE FANS WAKE UP ENGLAND IS A JOKE COMPARED TO ITALY AND SPAIN |url=https://soccergaming.com/forums/threads/all-you-premier-league-fans-wake-up-england-is-a-joke-compared-to-italy-and-spain.4657/ |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=Soccer Gaming |language=en-US}}</ref>

Additionally, nineteen players were nominated but received no votes: [[Tony Adams (footballer)|Tony Adams]] (Arsenal & England), [[Roberto Baggio]] (Bologna/Inter Milan & Italy), [[Zvonimir Boban]] (AC Milan & Croatia), [[Fabio Cannavaro]] (Parma & Italy), [[Denílson (footballer, born 1977)|Denílson]] (São Paulo/Real Betis & Brazil), [[Tore André Flo]] (Chelsea & Norway), [[Adrian Ilie]] (Valencia & Romania), [[Filippo Inzaghi]] (Juventus & Italy), [[Robert Jarni]] (Real Betis/Real Madrid & Croatia), [[Hidetoshi Nakata]] (Bellmare Hiratsuka/Perugia & Japan), [[Pavel Nedvěd]] (Lazio & Czech Republic), [[Sunday Oliseh]] (Ajax & Nigeria), [[Ariel Ortega]] (Valencia/Sampdoria & Argentina), [[Gianluca Pagliuca]] (Inter Milan & Italy), [[Marcelo Salas]] (River Plate/Lazio & Chile), [[David Seaman]] (Arsenal & England), [[Andriy Shevchenko]] (Dynamo Kyiv & Ukraine), [[Juan Sebastián Verón]] (Sampdoria/Parma & Argentina) and [[Iván Zamorano]] (Inter Milan & Chile).
